paragraphs.text: Dear elders and sisters, well, hope you had a great day today. I certainly had a great day. I'm looking forward to district conferences starting tomorrow. I understand we got a storm that's going to roll in sometime this week. Hopefully it won't be too big of a storm, but I'm looking forward to the rain, so I hope we're going to get some of that. That'll cool things off for sure. I know some of you are feeling pretty warm in your apartments. Just so that you know, my air conditioning is not working in the mission home that very well, so I feel a little the heat too. Don't shed any tears for me, though. I'm doing fine.

Alright, let's jump into our final episode of the drawing on the powers of heaven that we're going to deal with, because we'll be talking about this in more depth really through the district conferences. But this next, this next part that I want to share with you tonight is absolutely just jam-packed with nuggets of gold. There's just some real power stuff here that I have drawn upon in my life ever since I first read this book clear back when I was 19, 20 years old on a mission. I've been using this, I've worn through, so I'll bet I've purchased 40 copies of this book and read them and given them away and things like that. So this next little part is the part where it's all jammed together.

It starts out with the title Exert Yourself Mentally. The thought process itself is the key to increasing faith. To a great extent, we accomplish what we think about. In other words, what you think about today, tomorrow, or next month will mold your attitude and determine what you will accomplish during your life. Your life is influenced more by your thoughts than anything else. This is from Spencer W. Kimball, President Kimball: "How could a person possibly become what he's not thinking, nor is any thought, when persistently entertained, too small to have its effect. The divinity that shapes our ends is indeed in ourselves," close quote.

In order to exercise faith, once you have prayerfully selected a righteous desire—it could be something to do with your church calling, or something to do with your work, or your family, or your school, or any of these things—anyway, you must become totally focused on that desire. You got, you got to become preoccupied with it, thinking about it a lot. Faith can be gauged to a great extent by the amount of time you spend thinking about your righteous desire. If your, if your mind's just all over the place and doesn't really spend much time thinking about that thing that you're trying to achieve, it's not really a desire, it's not really a goal, and it's not really going to happen.

So don't confuse preoccupation, however, with worry or anxiety. That's not what we're talking about here. Preoccupation never is a function of anxiety or worry. When we're exercising faith, it's the opposite of anxiety. It's the opposite of worry because it's the opposite of fear. When your mind is dwelling on the adverse consequences or the negative things that might happen, you tend to get out of control, and we're trying to come back into control.

Recently, I had a letter from one of our foreign missionaries who went home and he wanted to know what his strengths and weaknesses are. And I said, "Elder, you should know me well enough by now to know I don't focus on weaknesses. I focus on strengths. We'll let the Lord take care of the weaknesses like he says that he will in Ether 12:27." Let's focus on getting our strengths going, and it's the same thing here. The mind is like a field. You will harvest whatever you plant in it if you nourish it. You should learn to follow the Lord's admonition: "Look unto me in every thought; doubt not, fear not." That's D&C 6:36.

Research has demonstrated that people use their minds in constructive thinking only about 10% of the time. Similarly, the amount of faith they exercise is very limited. We are commanded not to doubt: "Doubt not, but be believing." The interesting comment here, again this is from Joseph Smith: "...where doubt and uncertainty are, there faith is not, nor can it be; for doubt and faith do not exist in the same person at the same time; so that persons whose minds are under doubts and fears cannot have unshaken confidence; and where unshaken confidence is not, there faith is weak."

Thinking negatively does not require any effort. Maintaining a believing frame of mind, however, requires a lot of effort if you're going to do it over a sustained period of time, which is what we need to learn how and grow the capacity to do. By the process of faith, thoughts produce an effect as literal as physical exertion. Your thoughts—now get this—your thoughts, more than anything else, will be the determining factor in what you accomplish during your life. Exercising faith in the powers of heaven is a fairly simple process, but it involves continual mental exertion. As Joseph Smith said: "When a man works by faith he works by mental exertion instead of by physical force."

Mental exertion involves the following basic steps. Number one, you've got to train yourself to be conscious of your thoughts. And that sounds simple, and I'm telling you there's a lot of people think that's just silly, but then they think about things without even thinking they're thinking. Their mind's wandering all over the place, so you've got to learn how to be conscious of what you're thinking about. Number two, learn to investigate your thoughts to determine if they add to or weaken your faith. If it builds up your faith, that's great. If it weakens your faith, you go to step three: replace that thought immediately with a thought that is going to build up your faith, such as reminding yourself about the blessings that the Lord has given you or miracles you have experienced in your past, so forth and so on.

If you learn to put forth the necessary mental exertion, you'll be successful in cultivating the faith required to qualify for the power of heaven to be placed into your life. However, in order to exert yourself mentally, you must have power and dominion over your mind. You cannot allow your mind to be easily distracted or to focus on something that is extraneous to the purpose or object of your desired blessing. For instance, when you call upon the Lord for his blessings, do you find yourself thinking about other things you need to do, or other, you know, little things going on, or the dog barking next door, or, you know, whatever's happening in your apartment, or do you stay focused on the prayer? We'll talk more about this in the district conference this week.

The next time you pray or meditate, see if you have the power control of your mind sufficient to keep it from wandering during your attempt to communicate with the Lord. Just think about this. Consider how offensive it would be if you were talking to somebody and they were constantly looking around the room, you know, about everything and not paying any attention to what you were trying to say to them. Sometimes I think our prayers are a little bit like that. We may be saying some words, but our minds are a thousand kilometers away from what our words are saying to the Lord.

Until you learn to discipline your mind and have complete control over it, you'll be very limited in your capacity to exercise faith to power. The full power of the mind is only realized when it's specifically focused and directed to a specific end that you want to achieve. Matthew 6:22: "...if therefore thine eye [the mind's eye] be single, thy whole body shall be full of light." If you allow your mind to dwell randomly on incidental, mundane preoccupations, you're gonna be limited in your ability to draw the power of faith, and your mind will not be a source of power for you.

You will discover, however, that as you attempt to control and focus your mind, the devil will begin to bring things to your view to distract you. You can count on this, because he knows this is the secret key. If you can, if you can get this developed, he loses all of his ability to influence you. So he's gonna get real active when you start to develop this, but you know, if you bear in there and just keep focused on it, eventually he gets discouraged. Here's a quote that's been a part of my development for a long, long time. It's from President Brigham Young. Quote: "The greatest mystery a man ever learned is to know how to control the human mind and bring every faculty and power of it in subjection to Jesus Christ. This is the greatest mystery we have to learn while in these tabernacles of clay," or in other words, while in these mortal bodies.

You need to constantly, or consistently really, remind yourself that the mind is literally the key to unlocking the powers of heaven. You must learn to control your mind. You need to be able to control your mind so that it's not distracted by events or anything going on around you, and you just have to learn how to focus all of its force on a particular desire that you're trying to achieve. This quote from Elder Orson Pratt, one of the early Apostles, is very instructive. Quote: "If a person trains his mind to walk in the Spirit, and brings his whole mind to bear upon its operations, and upon the principles of faith which are calculated to put him in possession of the power of God, how much greater will be his facilities for obtaining knowledge.", close quote.

In our present society, music, television, movies have become like a drug for people's minds. Listening to good music is fine, but when a person turns to music as an escape for hours, or television, or movies, or watching videos on YouTube, or whatever, it becomes extremely detrimental. If a person spends hours observing sporting events but does not engage in any sort of physical exercise, his body will suffer. As it is with the body, so it is with the mind. If we allow our mind to just engage in things that don't require any effort, the mind just gets weaker and the ability to focus goes away.

One of the best ways to exert yourself mentally is to create a picture in your mind of the thing for which you're striving, and to repeatedly bring this picture to mind. Just keep forcing it back into your mind using your imagination. In a very literal sense, desired ends must be created spiritually in the mind before they can be realized physically. Through the process of faith, you can see clearly in your mind what you can accomplish with the Lord's help. Being allowed to see clearly what we can accomplish with the Lord's help is a form of a vision. Seeing things in your mind's eye is seeing with the eye of faith.

You can exert yourself mentally by asking yourself questions and then carefully weighing various answers, by exploring various solutions to a problem and carefully weighing the projected consequences of each alternative position. You can also exert yourself mentally by rehearsing things in your mind. This is what we see great athletes do all the time. They'll shoot the free throw in their mind. They'll even go through the motions of it before they actually shoot the ball. They're seeing that ball leave their hands and go all the way up, arching down and go through the net. This is something that great athletes have figured out many, many decades ago. But so many of the rest of us don't understand that seeing with the eye of faith is a very powerful thing and an essential thing to drawing down the powers of heaven.

It's important to take a little time every day. You know that I do with meditation, where you take the time to just visualize the way you want things to go that day, that week, that month, that year—the way you want things to go in your life—to visualize what you want to have happen and literally see it happening. And as you rehearse that over and over and over again, that's acting with the eye of faith. That's mental exertion, and that's what creates the ability for you to draw down the powers of heaven when what it is that you want is a righteous desire.

Now, people who don't make an exerted effort to control their thoughts, they have some other problems. Not only will they not achieve their goals, but they also tend to dwell on little stuff: resentments, offenses, jealousies, anxieties. They look for offenses. They look for ways to get involved in self-pity, because their mind's just wandering around aimlessly. Powerful discoveries, powerful insights are made by people who have learned how to discipline their minds to the extent that they can concentrate on one problem for long periods of time. This is what you see in the prophets and the great leaders of the Church. This is what you see in the great inventors, such as Sir Isaac Newton and Albert Einstein. People like this tend to be able to just concentrate on something, and they didn't get that by some kind of a gift. They earned it by practice over long periods of time, focusing, focusing, focusing until they literally can focus and the whole house is coming down around them and they're still focused.

We talked about this early on with the missionaries two and a half, nearly three years ago, as we did our practice teaching. We would do practice teaching with the idea of creating distractions to get the missionaries to learn how to not be distracted, to stay focused. As you concentrate on achieving your goals, your righteous desires, you continually remind yourself that if you exercise the necessary faith, the Lord will assist you in achieving them. Learning to think positively about something over a long period of time can be difficult because we have to form a new habit. Some of us have got these habits where we just kind of think about what can go wrong, but I want you to change that habit into a habit of what can go right. Start thinking about the positive things. Start visualizing the good things that are going to happen, because with the Lord's help you can do anything. I mean, you don't want to get into the Laman and Lemuel mindset; you want to stay in the Nephi mindset.

When you focus your thoughts on the achievement of righteous desires, you are serving the Lord with your heart, mind, and strength. Many members of the Church, unfortunately, only serve with their strength, their time, and their energy, but their mind is far away, their heart is far away. They tend not to use their willpower as much as they should, and then they wonder why they don't get all the blessings that they ought to get. It's because they're not single. They're not completely focused. They've got one part in and two or three parts out. What you think about is either going to build up your faith or it's going to weaken your faith, and that's why how you manage your thoughts is so incredibly important.

The power of faith through thought is either going to be concentrated by your focus or it's going to be diluted by your distraction. Your ability to draw on this power will increase, however, with effort. You may not be very good at it right now. You're probably not. I wasn't when I was your age. I was scattered all over the place like many people are at that stage of life. But as you practice staying focused—and we'll talk about this in district conference, an actual exercise for you to do this—as you practice exerting your control over your thoughts, your capacity to focus your mind increases.

Now, it's so important to realize that you can change your outward circumstances by changing your inward thinking. Literally, thoughts are things. Thoughts can literally, and usually do, become reality if they're nourished. "A man is literally what he thinks, his character being the complete sum of all of his thoughts," said by President Spencer W. Kimball. David O. McKay said this: "The thought in your mind at this moment is contributing, however infinitesimally, almost imperceptibly, to the shaping of your soul... Even passing in idle thoughts leave their impressions upon you." Another one from President David O. McKay: "I will know what you are if you tell me what you think about when you don't have to think." That one's in Preach My Gospel. I know you've seen that one before.

If you radically alter your thoughts, you will be blown away at how rapidly the material conditions in your life begin to be transformed. Your thoughts actually dictate, determine your circumstances, because thoughts govern habits, habits dictate circumstances. All actions, both spontaneous—those are the ones that just grow out of not even thinking about it—and those that think, are ultimately products of our thoughts. You exercise your agency in what you think about as literally as you do in your actions. In fact, I would say that agency only operates in the realm of thoughts. Once you've nourished the thought, once you've allowed your agency to be absent and you've just nourished the thought, it's going to act out and you can put all the energy into your agency on the physical side that you want to; you're still going to do that thing that you nourished in your mind. That's why the scriptures say: "For as he thinketh in his heart, so is he."

As you think in your mind and you nourish that thought, and you nourish it and you hold on to it and you focus on it, it drops from your mind into your heart, and when that happens, it's going to manifest itself in the physical world. It doesn't matter what you say. I've seen too many people who've allowed themselves to let thoughts drop from their heads into their hearts and then wondered why they couldn't stop themselves from doing something that they knew was going to be very self-destructive. It's also important to know that the Lord will judge us on our thoughts. He says in Alma 12:14, our thoughts will also condemn us. It's a very sobering thought to realize that every thought is being recorded and will be a critical factor in our final judgment. Thank goodness for the Atonement of Jesus Christ that allows us to repent of not just our actions but of our thoughts when necessary.

So as we conclude here, you're going to begin to feel the power of faith in your life when you have been successful in maintaining the necessary mental discipline, coupled with righteous living, for several consecutive weeks. You must resolve to make an exerted effort to exercise faith in your ability to draw on the powers of heaven over a sustained period of time. You will never experience the power of faith to any great extent unless you're willing to maintain your efforts over time. This is not a sprint. This is a marathon.

So resolve to test this principle by putting forth the necessary effort even though it's difficult. And this is the key element: nothing any good is easy. Nothing. So if it's easy, what you're doing right now, trust me, it will not take you someplace you want to go, because nothing that's easy will lead to something that's good. It's just not organized that way in God's universe. So when you're going uphill, when you're battling to keep moving to higher ground, you can automatically assume you're on the right path. Mental exertion is exertion, no less than physical exertion is exertion. Physical exertion, well, that's the phase one. But phase two, the advanced course, is learning how to use your mind and to exercise it in the pursuit of your righteous desires. I'm excited to share this information with you in our district conference starting tomorrow. I love you all, elders and sisters. Have a great night.
